doc.title: Ray Shiner interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 11, 1998

title: Faking medleys, pay, personnel and labels
summary: Small library, fake medleys, $125-150 a week, great sidemen, RCA then United Artists.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: And of course we started out with 42 numbers in the library, but every time the band — we all had different backgrounds. Some of us had strictly classical backgrounds, some
both, and some jazz backgrounds. We had great jazz musicians in the band. And we used to fake, well we’d play medleys, fake medleys.
To get through the gig. It was probably that — you start me talking and I won’t stop, it’s the happiest days of my life.
That’s okay. That’s why we’re here. I mean can you tell me what you were making on that band?
I started making a hundred and a quarter. I got a raise to a hundred and fifty. That was a lot of money.

I didn’t care if it paid ten cents. I was a member of — I still brag about it today, I was a member of the original Sauter-Finegan Orchestra. And I don’t care about the money. None of us did. We had world famous jazz musicians. Mundell Lowe played guitar, Nick Travis played trumpet, Joe Ferrante played trumpet, Sonny Russo played — you know we had great musicians on that band.
And what label did you record on?
RCA. But toward the end we recorded for United Artists — UA.
